rules.comment: Public-transit ride (REQ-RULE-016): title 'Ride to <station>', text '5 stops · 10 min', subText 'Arrive 20:26'. TRANSIT with the stop count, the station as the road line and the ETA; unmatched, the watch showed nothing for the whole ride (real capture, 2026-09). Above google-maps-arrive-en: it is anchored to a leading 'Ride to', so a station named like 'Destination Park' must not read as ARRIVE.

Boarding a transit line (REQ-RULE-016): title 'Take the 197' / 'Get on the 851', text '<stop> · Departs 19:57', subText 'Arrive 20:24'. TRANSIT; the road line is the line and the stop with its departure on two lines. Needs 'Departs' in text, so 'Take the exit' or 'Take the pedestrian crossing' never read as transit. Shared by a user as custom rules (real capture, en-US, Android 16, Google Maps 26.41, 2026-10).

Last leg of a ride (REQ-RULE-016): title 'Get off at <stop>', text 'Next stop · 2 min'. TRANSIT with 1 stop left. Shared by a user as custom rules (real capture, en-US, Android 16, 2026-10). Above google-maps-arrive-en, so a stop named like 'Destination Park' stays transit.

'Get off at <stop>' without 'Next stop' (synthetic, following the captured card): TRANSIT, with the stop count when the text carries one ('3 stops · 6 min'). One step below google-maps-transit-get-off-next-stop-en.

Title only, and never the bare word 'arrive'. Google Maps puts the ETA in subText ('Arrive 23:51') on EVERY navigation notification, so matching combinedText here classified every turn as ARRIVE (real capture, 2026-07-13).

Walking, last stretch: ProgressStyle card, title 'Arrive in 1 min (70 m)', text '<destination>'. No turns remain, so ARRIVE with the distance to the destination; unmatched, the watch kept the last turn card ('0 m, turn right') for minutes (real capture, 2026-09). Just below google-maps-arrive-en, above every maneuver rule, so a destination name with a maneuver word cannot win. '1 min' never parses as a distance.

Walking between turns: ProgressStyle card, title 'Walk 7 min (500 m)', text 'Arrive 18:57 · <destination>'. Continue toward the destination, with its ETA. Deliberately NO distance: the metres are the whole remaining walk, not the distance to the next turn, and under an arrow they would read as 'turn in 500 m' (real capture, 2026-09).

Classic layout of google-maps-roundabout-en: title is the bare distance ('50 m'), text the instruction. Same maneuver, but the road line takes the instruction from text; the base rule's title-first primaryText showed the distance twice (real walking capture, 2026-09). One priority step above the base rule so it wins whenever the title is only a distance.

Classic layout of google-maps-use-lane-left-en: title is the bare distance, text the instruction, so the road line comes from text.

Lane guidance: 'Use the left lane to merge onto <road>' / 'Use the left 2 lanes to take the <road> ramp'. Treated like keep left (SLIGHT_LEFT). Unmatched before (real en-US capture, Belgium, 2026-09). Priority 90, below the turn rules, so 'Use the right lane to turn left' still shows a left turn.
Classic layout of google-maps-use-lane-right-en: title is the bare distance, text the instruction, so the road line comes from text.

Lane guidance: 'Use the right lane to merge onto <road>' / 'Use the right 2 lanes to take the <road> ramp'. Treated like keep right (SLIGHT_RIGHT). Unmatched before (real en-US capture, Belgium, 2026-09). Priority 90, below the turn rules, so 'Use the right lane to turn left' still shows a left turn.

Classic layout of google-maps-take-exit-left-en: title is the bare distance ('350 m'), text the instruction. One priority step above the base rule so the road line takes the instruction, not the distance.

Motorway exit on the left: 'Take exit 12 on the left toward <road>'. One step above google-maps-take-exit-en, which assumes the usual right-hand exit. Synthetic, from the right-hand form in a real capture (#95).
Classic layout of google-maps-take-exit-en: title is the bare distance ('350 m'), text the instruction. One priority step above the base rule so the road line takes the instruction, not the distance.

Motorway exit: '0.7 mi · Take exit 425 toward <road>' (real capture, en-US, Android 17, 2026-10, #95); the destination-approach fallback showed it as ARRIVE before. Right-hand unless 'on the left' (google-maps-take-exit-left-en). Below lane (90), turn (100) and keep (120), so their side wins; roundabout (190) keeps 'take the 2nd exit'. Distance from the title only: a title-less classic card's subText holds the trip total.
Classic layout of google-maps-merge-en: title is the bare distance ('350 m'), text the instruction. One priority step above the base rule so the road line takes the instruction, not the distance.

Highway merge: '350 ft · Merge onto I-35E' (real capture, en-US, Android 17, 2026-10, #95). Before this rule the destination-approach fallback showed it as ARRIVE. The card doesn't say the side, so straight on. Below the lane rules (90): 'Use the left lane to merge onto <road>' stays SLIGHT_LEFT.

Classic layout of google-maps-exit-parking-en: title is the bare distance ('350 m'), text the instruction. One priority step above the base rule so the road line takes the instruction, not the distance.
The step a route opens with when starting from a car park: 'Exit the parking lot toward <road>' (real capture, en-US, Android 17, 2026-10, #95). Straight on, like 'Head toward <road>'.
Classic layout of google-maps-take-the-en: title is the bare distance ('50 m'), text the instruction, so the road line comes from text (#56). One priority step above the base rule.

Walking steps 'Take the pedestrian crossing' (real capture, en-GB, Android 17, 2026-10, #56) and the same family (crosswalk, stairs, footbridge, underpass, lift/elevator, escalator; synthetic, validate against captures): straight on with the distance and ETA. Just above google-maps-continue-en and below every turn, keep, lane and roundabout rule, so a turn word still wins and 'Take the 2nd exit' stays a roundabout.

Classic layout of google-maps-continue-en: title is the bare distance ('50 m'), text the instruction. Same maneuver, but the road line takes the instruction from text; the base rule's title-first primaryText showed the distance twice (real walking capture, 2026-09). One priority step above the base rule so it wins whenever the title is only a distance.

Covers the step Google Maps opens a route with: 'Head toward <road>' / 'Head east on <road>' (real capture, 2026-07-13). Walking says 'Walk towards <road>' / 'Walk east on <road>' instead (#51, real capture, 2026-10); 'walk' needs towards/on/a direction next, so the 'Walk 7 min' overview card never matches here.

Classic layout: title = distance ('220 m'), text = a bare 'toward <road>' with no verb, so google-maps-continue-en misses it (real captures, 2026-07-30). A bare heading is continue-straight. Distance from the title ONLY: without a title, combinedText's first number+unit is the trip total in subText ('166 km'). ETA from the classic subText '28 min · 12 km · 23:14 ETA' (#95).

Final approach: near the destination Google Maps shows the place name as the step, '90 m · <place>' (route-capture harness, Android 17, 2026-10, #66). ARRIVE with the distance. A fallback, so lowest priority and English only. A step starting with a maneuver verb ('Take exit …', 'Merge onto …') is excluded: before #95 an unknown verb landed here and showed the arrival flag on the motorway; now it stays unmatched and shows in diagnostics.
